measurement.title: Measurement - perceptual accuracy (color difference)
measurement.subtitle: How accurately a model represents human color DIFFERENCE. Every entrant scores with its OWN ΔE on all of it: difference prediction = STRESS (+CI95 on hover); discrimination / 3-D / tolerance = JND-ellipse roundness (a pure distance model like metricspace or CIEDE2000 is scored with its own distance on the same ellipses, not blank). Overall = one equal vote per difference + discrimination + 3-D + tolerance dataset. Lower = better; grey appearance diagnostics are shown not scored (they need forward coordinates, which distance models lack).
measurement.holdout_note: metricspace is fit to COMBVD, so its BFD-P/Leeds/Witt/RIT scores may be in-sample; on the held-out MacAdam 1974 it does NOT win (CAM16-UCS does). Overfit Δrank (metricspace only) = held-out rank - mean in-sample rank.

generation.title: Generation - color-synthesis quality
generation.subtitle: Only generation-relevant properties: hue-constancy (gradients & shades keep their hue) and even spacing (no banding), plus a physics robustness gate. Difference / discrimination metrics live on the Measurement board - they judge color-matching, not generation. Lower = better.
